draft.title: Precipitation reactions
card: A precipitation reaction happens when two solutions are mixed and the ions combine to form an insoluble solid. The solid is called the precipitate.
In the mixture, the ions swap partners. A new combination of cation and anion forms. If that compound is insoluble, it comes out of solution as a solid.
Solubility rules tell you which ionic compounds dissolve in water. For example, nitrates and sodium salts are soluble, while silver chloride and lead(II) iodide are insoluble.
Ions that stay dissolved are spectator ions. The net ionic equation leaves them out: Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) → AgCl(s).
draft.remember: Swap the partners, then check the solubility rules: an insoluble product is the precipitate.

a.q: Solutions of silver nitrate and sodium chloride are mixed and a white solid forms. What is the white solid?
a.why: The ions swap partners to give silver chloride and sodium nitrate. Silver chloride is insoluble, so it forms the solid. Sodium nitrate is soluble, because all nitrates are, so it stays dissolved.
a.clue: Swap the partners, then ask which new compound is insoluble.

b.q: Mia mixes solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide. Which ions are the spectator ions?
b.why: Lead(II) iodide is insoluble, so lead(II) and iodide ions join to form the precipitate. Potassium and nitrate ions stay dissolved and do not change, so they are spectators. Lead(II) and nitrate ions are not a pair: they come from the same starting solution, but only lead(II) goes on to form the solid.
b.clue: Spectator ions are the ones that are not in the solid.
